name: Lodge reports, notices, permits and disputes with regulators
summary: Supports lodging reports, notices, permits and disputes with regulators. Reads regulator correspondence from the compliance mailbox, logs each item in a lodgement register with its due date, and drafts reminders for the owner. Crons read and draft; a person makes every lodgement in the regulator's portal and approves every email.

regulator-lodgement.evidence: 16 worklist calls were read, none described steps or variants. The steps come from the ASIC, NHVR and QBCC vendor docs, which map each step but no operations.

covered_by.deadline-check: reminders (due dates come from the business's notice rules; the regulator docs give none)
covered_by.gather-information: gap (the docs do not list what a lodgement needs; a person gathers it)
covered_by.prepare-report: gap (portal forms are filled in by a person)
covered_by.check-content: gap (a person checks figures and wording)
covered_by.internal-approval: register (an internal note to the owner, approved before it is sent)
covered_by.lodge-online: gap (no regulator portal is mapped; a person lodges)
covered_by.pay-fee: gap (portal payments are a person's job)
covered_by.receive-confirmation: intake (confirmation emails in the mailbox are read and logged)
covered_by.objection-or-dispute: gap (the docs do not describe objections; a person decides)
covered_by.outcome-and-follow-up: reminders (open items stay on the register until a person marks them Lodged)
covered_by.record-keeping: register (one row per notice, written as a draft)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: Read regulator notices that arrived in the compliance mailbox.

crons.name: register
crons.summary: Log each new notice in the lodgement register and queue an internal note to the owner.

crons.name: reminders
crons.summary: Queue a reminder to the owner for each open lodgement due within the window (22:00 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

draft_ops_note: Reads, a register row and an Outlook draft to the owner. None of them leaves the business. Sending the draft to the owner is the one live operation, and only a person can approve it.

microsoft-365.covers: compliance mailbox intake, lodgement register rows, owner drafts and their approved send

gaps: ASIC, NHVR and QBCC: lodgement, forms, fees, confirmations and objections happen in each regulator's own portal. None of those portals has operations in the kit, so no adapter exists and a person lodges.
Regulator deadlines: the ASIC, NHVR and QBCC docs give no lodgement dates. The business sets each due window in notice_rules.
The kit has no operation that updates a register row. A person marks an item Lodged in Excel, and the reminders stop only then.
Judgment steps stay with a person: gathering information, preparing and checking the report, responding to a regulator, and any objection or dispute.
Intake depends on the search word. A regulator notice that does not carry it is not read.
The Microsoft 365 adapter is docs-only: it has not run against a tenant. Field names come from the Microsoft Graph OpenAPI spec in endpoint-map/raw/microsoft-365.
Excel may reformat a typed date on write. The reminder reads a text date or a serial number, and a sandbox run should confirm the Due column comes back in either form.

evidence.calls: 16 worklist calls read, none rejected; the evidence file holds no steps, variants or tools for this workflow
evidence.platforms: ASIC, NHVR and QBCC vendor docs mapped step by step; none has operations in the kit. Microsoft 365 is the only mapped platform used, for the mailbox and the register.
